title: Day 604 — Mexico Expels Two CIA Agents Who Operated Without Accreditation in Chihuahua Anti-Drug Operation
detail: On May 28, 2026 (Day 604), President Sheinbaum confirmed at her morning mañanera that Mexico has expelled two CIA agents who participated without proper accreditation in the April 19, 2026 anti-drug operation in Chihuahua that dismantled a clandestine synthetic drug laboratory. The operation resulted in the deaths of two CIA agents (Richard Leiter Johnston III and John Dudley Black) and two Mexican AEI investigators; the other two surviving CIA agents entered Mexico legally but did not register their intelligence activities with federal authorities — a violation of Mexican law and sovereignty protocols. Mexico issued a formal diplomatic note requesting the two surviving agents leave the country; they complied. Sheinbaum framed the expulsion as a sovereignty enforcement action rather than a hostile diplomatic move: 'They entered the country with legal status, but they did not register their intelligence activities as required — that is the line that was crossed.' BACKGROUND: The CIA-Chihuahua incident triggered a broader investigation that revealed at least three additional unauthorized CIA operations in Chihuahua during 2026 without federal notification (reported by the Los Angeles Times on April 27). The probe implicated Chihuahua state officials — particularly Governor María Eugenia 'Maru' Campos (PAN) — who allegedly facilitated the unauthorized bilateral security collaboration outside constitutional federal channels. Chihuahua State AG Jáuregui Moreno resigned April 28; Campos refused a Senate summons and was subsequently subpoenaed by the FGR as a witness (scheduled appearance May 27). At the same mañanera, Sheinbaum addressed Governor Campos' FGR summons: 'All Mexicans must understand that collaboration with a foreign government has constitutional limits — sovereignty is not optional.' DIPLOMATIC CONTEXT: The expulsion comes just as USMCA Round 1 formal bilateral negotiations opened in Mexico City (May 28–29), creating parallel tracks of security confrontation and trade cooperation in US-Mexico relations. U.S. officials have not publicly commented on the expulsion. The incident is the most concrete sovereignty-enforcement action of the Sheinbaum administration against the United States.

media.caption: Sheinbaum confirms Mexico expelled two CIA agents who operated without accreditation in Chihuahua anti-drug operation — framed as sovereignty enforcement

title: Day 604 — USMCA Round 1 Formally Opens in Mexico City: Ebrard and Deputy USTR Goettman Launch Bilateral Trade Talks
detail: On May 28, 2026 (Day 604), the first formal USMCA Joint Review bilateral negotiating round began at Mexico's Ministry of Economy in Mexico City — the most significant trade diplomatic event since the EU-Mexico summit on May 22. DELEGATIONS: Mexico's side was led by Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard, supported by Ministry of Economy trade negotiators. The U.S. delegation was led by Deputy USTR Ambassador Jeff Goettman; USTR Jamieson Greer had been expected to attend in person on May 27 but was recalled to Washington by President Trump and joined by video call instead. The U.S. team included a bipartisan delegation from the House Ways and Means Committee and approximately 60 business sector representatives. ROUND 1 AGENDA (May 28–29): The two-day session focused on: (1) Economic security framework and supply-chain resilience provisions to reduce dependence on non-USMCA-origin inputs; (2) Rules of origin for key industrial goods — particularly automotive and electronics — with U.S. demands for stricter content requirements to prevent Chinese-origin components from qualifying for USMCA zero-tariff treatment; (3) Chinese nearshoring restrictions and investment screening in critical sectors including semiconductors, batteries, and telecom equipment. EBRARD ASSESSMENT: Economy Secretary Ebrard acknowledged publicly that formal negotiations at this stage make a clean 16-year extension by the July 1, 2026 USMCA Joint Review deadline unlikely — more probable is a provisional agreement with continued negotiations on contested chapters. Mexico's core demands remain: elimination of Section 232 steel and aluminum tariffs, digital trade modernization, and clean energy provisions. DIPLOMATIC LEVERAGE: Mexico entered Round 1 with enhanced diplomatic standing following the signing of the EU-Mexico Modernised Global Agreement and Interim Trade Agreement on May 22 — reducing structurally one-sided U.S. dependence. Round 2 is scheduled June 16–17 in Washington D.C. (agriculture, labor standards); Round 3 in the week of July 20 in Mexico City (final consolidation).

media.caption: USMCA Round 1 formally opens in Mexico City — Ebrard leads Mexico's delegation as Goettman (Deputy USTR) leads U.S. side; focus on rules of origin and Chinese nearshoring restrictions

title: Day 604 — Mañanera: Sheinbaum Publishes Asset Declaration; CNTE Dialogue Continues; Rocha Moya FGR Update
detail: Additional highlights from President Sheinbaum's May 28, 2026 Day 604 mañanera: (1) ASSET DECLARATION PUBLISHED: Sheinbaum's 2026 patrimonial declaration was released, showing net annual income of 1,791,441 pesos — essentially entirely from her presidential salary. She reported an 8% minority stake in two manufacturing companies ('Eli Cami y Cia' and 'Sintacrom de México'), which are family business holdings. The declaration aligns with obligations under the General Law of Responsibilities of Public Servants. Critics noted that presidential salaries under the 4T austerity framework are capped at 102,000 pesos monthly. (2) ROCHA MOYA / FGR UPDATE: Security Secretary García Harfuch explained at the mañanera why Sinaloa Governor Rubén Rocha Moya was not detained despite appearing before the FGR and having an Interpol red notice: the FGR is still gathering evidence before seeking an arrest warrant — the legal standard for detention requires the federal attorney general to formally request pretrial detention from a judge, which had not yet occurred. Rocha Moya appeared before the FGR on May 26–27 alongside Senator Enrique Inzunza Cazárez and other co-accused in the Los Chapitos conspiracy indictment. Sheinbaum stated: 'The FGR will provide updates on the case when there are developments.' (3) CNTE STRIKE — DIALOGUE CONTINUES: Sheinbaum characterized the CNTE action as involving 'some teachers, not all,' and confirmed working dialogue tables between the SEP (Education Secretariat) and SEGOB (Interior) with CNTE representatives remain active. Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez confirmed a second meeting with CNTE Section 22 (Oaxaca). The CNTE's formal strike and mega-march toward Mexico City's Zócalo remains set for June 1, 2026 — during the FIFA World Cup's opening weekend. (4) ECONOMIC INDICATORS: Sheinbaum highlighted 12 positive economic indicators presented during the week, including Q1 2026 record FDI ($23.6B), declining inflation (4.11% vs 4.45% April), and an updated unemployment figure of 2.5% — a slight improvement from January's 2.7%. (5) FIFA WORLD CUP TICKETS: Sheinbaum announced she will give away her presidential inauguration match tickets from a contest aimed at young women and girls who love soccer — following through on a commitment she made publicly in the weeks before the tournament.

media.caption: Day 604 mañanera: Sheinbaum's 2026 asset declaration published; García Harfuch explains Rocha Moya non-detention; CNTE dialogue tables continue ahead of June 1 mega-march
